subject: Private deployment BYOK: cross-border handshake proposal
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deployment BYOK: cross-border handshake proposal

Hi Samantha / Acme procurement team,

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our discussion, I’m sending a short proposal for the BYOK (customer-managed key) handshake and how we can safely support a US-hosted private deployment while allowing limited, auditable customer key operations that Acme needs for compliance. This is deliberately lightweight — we want to capture the operational boundary, evidence we can provide, and a suggested mutual action plan.

Summary (high-level):
- Deployment mode: VPC private deployment (Redwood control plane in Red region; compute isolated in Acme VPC)
- Key model: Customer supplies CMK in their KMS (BYOK). Redwood will not hold plaintext keys. Redwood will be authorised via a short-lived, scoped delegation to encrypt/decrypt on compute nodes only.
- Cross-border constraint: No customer plaintext or unencrypted payload will be exported from Acme-controlled VPC. Logs/evidence will be redacted and geo-filtered per Acme’s EU/US routing table.

Attachments: I’ve attached a 2-page handshake proposal (RDW-privdep-byok-handshake-proposal-v1.pdf) with diagrams, and a suggested mutual action plan (MAP) spreadsheet.

Next steps I propose:
1) Acme to confirm the approved KMS ARNs and which service accounts may request key operations.
2) Redwood legal/ops to provide a short DPA annex with the BYOK delimited responsibilities and operator access exceptions.
3) Run a short proof-of-concept (2 weeks) to capture audit evidence and trace a sample request flow.

Questions for Acme: can you confirm whether your procurement/legal team will require Redwood to add a key custody clause or whether the existing DPA + annex will suffice? Also, do you expect escrow of key material (we typically do not support escrow for BYOK; we can propose an HSM-backed third party if needed).

Irene / Laura / Priyom — looping you in for technical/contract comments.

Thanks,
Rishi
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference

--
Attachments: RDW-privdep-byok-handshake-proposal-v1.pdf (2 pages, diagram), mutual-action-plan-acme-20250317.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Samantha King <samantha.king@acmehealth.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>, K. Patel <k.patel@kensu.com>
Date: Fri, 14 Mar 2025 12:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment BYOK: cross-border handshake proposal

Rishi —

Thanks for the clear summary and the diagram. A few clarifying questions from Acme before we draft our internal ask:

1) When you say "short-lived, scoped delegation" — can you confirm the maximum TTL you expect for the delegated credential and whether it is auditable by us?
2) We need to understand what telemetry Redwood will retain inside the private VPC vs what will be sent to Redwood control plane. Specifically: request traces, prompt/response metadata, and error stacks.
3) On escrow — our security team prefers an escrow option for a critical regulatory review; can Redwood point to a third-party HSM partner you have validated?

We’ve attached a high-level redline of the existing DPA (acme-redlines-20250316.pdf) highlighting BYOK language we’d like clarified. Also copied our retained consultant K. Patel to help scope operational evidence.

If okay, procurement would like a short call on Monday to align on the MAP and confirm timelines.

Best,
Samantha King
Head of INFSEC Programs
Acme Health

--
Attachments: acme-redlines-20250316.pdf (customer redlines)

From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Samantha King <samantha.king@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Mar 2025 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment BYOK: cross-border handshake proposal

Hi all — quick legal/ops notes after reviewing Rishi’s proposal and Acme’s redlines.

On TTL / delegated credential: our runtime issues short-lived service tokens that are scoped to the compute instance and operation. Typical TTL is 15 minutes; tokens are single-use for key operations and logged. We can increase audit verbosity (per-request signed audit record) for the POC.

Telemetry separation: we propose the following boundary:
- Within Acme VPC (compute + ephemeral KV): full request payloads (prompts/responses) and debug traces remain. Redwood will collect only operational metrics (latency, tokens served) and health telemetry from the control plane, and any aggregate error rates. No raw prompts or model outputs will be exported.

Escrow option: Redwood does not hold customer key material under BYOK. For customers who insist on escrow, we can integrate with a certified escrow provider (we have a vetted list; Kensu is acceptable as an assessor but is not an escrow provider). We recommend Thales/CyberSafe partner (example: Thales nShield, vendor escrow via specialized MSP). If Acme wants Redwood to contractually require an escrow provider, we can propose language but it will be an addendum to the DPA and will have extra fees.

Operational proof points we can provide for the POC:
- Signed per-request audit records (append-only) stored in Acme’s logging bucket
- Sample access logs showing TTL token issuance and the ephemeral compute identity that performed key ops
- Telemetry manifest showing fields sent to control plane (we'll redact any PII by default)

Rishi/Laura — please propose DPA annex language that captures these boundaries: BYOK responsibilities, token TTL, telemetry whitelist, and escrow carve-out. Priyom — coordinate with infra to capture the sample log format for the POC.

Thanks,
Irene
Senior Counsel, Legal Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Samantha King <samantha.king@acmehealth.com>, procurement@acmehealth.com
Cc: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>, K. Patel <k.patel@kensu.com>
Date: Mon, 17 Mar 2025 16:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private deployment BYOK: cross-border handshake proposal

Samantha — thanks for the quick review and the redlines. Quick update & proposed schedule: 

1) TTL and audit: We confirm 15-minute TTL as default for delegated tokens; for the POC we will enable per-request signed audit records and deliver them to the Acme logging bucket on request.
2) Telemetry: Redwood will ship only operational metrics to the control plane. We will provide a telemetry manifest before the kickoff and include sample logs during the POC.
3) Escrow: We can propose a list of validated HSM/escrow providers (Thales partner options) and include optional addendum language.

Attached: proposed DPA annex draft (RDW-dpa-annex-byok-v1.docx) and the MAP with proposed milestones (mutual-action-plan-acme-20250317.xlsx). I’ve also attached a customer-facing playbook excerpt that illustrates the request flow and the redaction points.

Proposed timeline:
- Wed 19 Mar: 30-min alignment call to confirm MAP and telemetry manifest (we’ll send calendar hold)
- Mon 24 Mar: kickoff POC (2 weeks) with delivery of signed audit samples by end of POC

If procurement is good with this cadence we’ll have our legal team send a clean annex and the technical runbook for review.

Next actions (short):
- Samantha to confirm availability for Wed 19 Mar call and whether procurement needs a PO in advance.
- K. Patel: please flag any missing evidence items for the MAP.

Appreciate it — looking forward to getting this over the finish line.

Best,
Rishi
Head of Privacy & Compliance
Redwood Inference
